chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who comes to me, so I buy goods for him from people and guarantee [the price/value] for him, then he comes to me with the dirhams, so I take them, then I withhold them from their owner, and I take the good dirhams and give [him] inferior ones in exchange. He said: 'If he guarantees [the debt/value], perhaps strictness is imposed upon him; he hurries [to pay] before taking [the goods], and withholds [the payment] after taking [the goods], so there is no objection to it.'

key_terms.فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: So there is no objection to it / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on an agent guaranteeing a purchase and exchanging currency while withholding payment from the seller?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the permissibility of an agent guaranteeing a purchase while withholding payment to exchange superior currency for inferior, noting that the guarantee (*daman*) subjects the agent to stricter accountability (*shaddid*), justifying the delay. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between simple agency (*wakalah*) and guaranteed transactions (*daman*), where the risk allocation influences the permissibility of holding funds. The principle underscores that financial guarantees carry inherent liabilities that allow for flexible settlement terms, a key concept in Islamic commercial law.
